“South Africa has openly racist ownership laws and is actively promoting white genocide.”

— Elon Musk, repeatedly calling out the South African government’s policies
South Africa is sliding deeper into institutionalized racism under the current government.

Instead of building a non-racial democracy after apartheid, the ANC and its allies have doubled down on race-based policies:

•  Expropriation Without Compensation — Laws allowing the seizure of land (mostly white-owned farms) without paying the owners.
•  B-BBEE racial quotas — Discriminatory rules in employment, ownership, and contracts that explicitly disadvantage non-Black citizens.
•  Farm attacks — Thousands of white farmers murdered since 1994, often with extreme brutality. The government downplays the racial motive while senior politicians chant “Kill the Boer.”
Elon Musk, who was born and raised in South Africa, has been one of the few high-profile voices calling this out for what it is: reverse racism that punishes competence and success based on skin color.
He has warned that South Africa is repeating the same mistakes Zimbabwe made under Mugabe — land seizures, economic collapse, and rising violence.
Instead of addressing crime, corruption, failing infrastructure, and economic decline, the government chooses to demonize successful citizens and push racial division.
Elon’s stance is simple: racism in any direction is wrong. A successful South Africa should be based on merit, rule of law, and unity — not resentment and redistribution by race.
The country had a historic chance after 1994. It’s now choosing the opposite path.
